_comment: The tier-label → pricing-level contract, shared between this repo and events-engine.
The same buyer is priced twice: the CMS quotes them from a HubDB row (HubL macros in
src/shared/utils/memberPricing.ts) and the Worker re-resolves the price at reserve
(toCanonicalMemberLevel in events-engine packages/worker/src/membership.ts). If the two
disagree the buyer is either refused ('the course price changed before checkout', when
the Worker resolves higher) or silently undercharged (when it resolves lower).
They cannot share code across two repos, so they share this table. Both sides have a
copy and a test asserting their own implementation reproduces it:
The two files are byte-identical apart from this comment's paths, so a drift is a diff.
CHANGING A LEVEL HERE CHANGES WHAT A CUSTOMER PAYS. Both repos ship together or the
disagreement this table exists to prevent is the thing you have just shipped.
'level' is the canonical pricing level. The column each level reads, and the
member → individual → non-member fallback when that column is blank, is asserted

labels.note: No tier known. The generic member column, never individual.

labels.label: corporate_gold
labels.note: snake_case key, not a display label

labels.label: Apprentice Member
labels.note: student is tested before the member fallthrough

labels.label: Individual Member
labels.note: 'individual' matches first, so this is unaffected by the bare-member rule below

labels.label: Member
labels.note: The drift this table was written after: the CMS sent bare 'member' to individual, the Worker to member.

labels.label: Corporate Member
labels.note: Same. Contains 'member' and none of the level keywords.

labels.label: Platinum
labels.note: Unknown label. Both sides must end on the generic member COLUMN; the Worker's internal level string for an unknown label is the label itself, which columnForLevel maps to the member column, so compare columns here and not level strings.
